particulars: All names, dates, places, store names, dollar amounts, physical measurements, print-point counts, sentence length, court and agency names, and statute titles are absent.

items.record: The case is a criminal prosecution of one man for armed robbery that ends in a wrongful-conviction reversal: 'charged him with two counts of armed robbery'.
items.reading: An agency's official self-review of its conduct toward families, for example in child welfare or benefits.
items.loss: The basic nature of the matter and the institution involved is misidentified.

items.record: The conviction rested on a fingerprint examiner's report that falsely said a database search had been done: 'they were loaded but never searched, although his report said they had been.'
items.reading: A coherent bureaucratic narrative that 'does not lie in any obvious way'.
items.loss: The specific mechanism of fabrication, a false statement of procedure by a technical expert, is missed.

items.record: Witness identifications were shaky and suggestive: a witness picked him on a second look at '80 percent', and another said 'an officer pointed to Brown's photo and asked whether she was sure it wasn't him'.
items.loss: The evidentiary process by which police steered eyewitnesses toward a suspect is lost.

items.record: Physical descriptions did not fit the accused: he was 'stocky', 'pudgy', 6 feet to 6 feet 2, while Brown was recorded as 5 feet 9 and 150 pounds with a full beard.
items.loss: The concrete mismatch between the suspect and the evidence that later underpinned innocence is missing.

items.record: The jury split its verdicts and convicted on one count only after the judge urged unanimity: 'acquitted Brown of the Family Dollar robbery and convicted him of the Dollar Tree robbery.'
items.loss: The trial dynamic of a divided jury pushed toward a verdict is absent.

items.record: The trial evidence was destroyed and the challenge failed for lack of bad faith: 'no proof the clerk had acted in bad faith.'
items.reading: Drift from harm to whether procedure was followed, framed as the institution's rationalization.
items.loss: The concrete step-by-step sequence of evidence loss and the court's legal test for it are not recovered.

items.record: The defense, not the state, forced the database search by going to the agency that runs it: 'Brown's lawyers confirmed with the State Bureau of Investigation... that the three prints were still in the system.'
items.reading: A counter-force of families, advocates, journalists, or a review body contesting a document.
items.loss: Who drove the correction, an innocence-project legal team using discovery, and how they did it is misdescribed.

items.record: The search identified another man as the likely source: 'one of the three prints came from a man identified as Daris J.... who was taller and heavier than Brown.'
items.loss: The alternative-perpetrator discovery that broke the case is missing.

items.record: The examiner's wider work was later reviewed for errors: 'instances where Mr. Babb had found a print did not have evidentiary value, but another analyst determined the same print did have evidentiary value.'
items.loss: The internal audit exposing a pattern in the expert's errors is missing.

items.record: The state consented while still defending trial counsel: 'maintaining that Brown's trial lawyer had been effective.'
items.reading: Resolution likely partial, with an official version persisting beside a counter-record.
items.loss: The actual outcome, a full dismissal achieved through a partial state concession, is misjudged.

items.record: The sequence spans arrest, conviction, appeal, release, and finally dismissal over more than a decade: 'the state dismissed the charge against Brown.'
items.reading: Escalation poised at a threshold, outcome undetermined.
items.loss: The completed long-run sequence and its end state are not recovered.

items.record: The accused's own position was steady denial resting on stable work and family ties: 'I had a full-time job and custody of my son.'
items.reading: Families feeling misdescribed by an authoritative text.
items.loss: The individual defendant's standpoint and his alibi-like circumstances are replaced by a collective family frame.
